title: Arkwave — Open model fit and runtime routing discovery
summary: Discovery call with Arkwave engineering and ML leads to evaluate open models and deployment modes. Primary goals: choose model family for customer service/triage products with long context (meeting transcripts + docs), multilingual (EN/ES/JA), and tool-calling to internal ticketing DB. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, KV cache, batching, expected QPS, and benchmarking next steps.
action_items: Samir to share Redwood pricing + perf spreadsheet and example rollout plan by 2028-07-22
Priya to send 10 sample transcripts, 5 multilingual prompts, and expected p95 latency target by 2028-07-21
Nadia to schedule an on-prem architecture deep-dive (SE-only) for week of 2028-07-30
Diego to confirm compliance controls required (SOC2/ISO/KMS) and share with Samir by 2028-07-24
next_steps: Redwood to run a small bench (hosted) against Arkwave prompt set (baseline Open-weights) and return results
Pilot scoping: 2-week POC on Dedicated GPUs for 32k context; Redwood to propose config
Schedule security questionnaire handoff and NDA addendum for on-prem testing
transcript: [00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick intros, we got Tom, Priya, Diego from Arkwave and Nadia and me from Redwood. How's the time?

[00:14] Tom - Arkwave (CTO): Good, thanks. We've been digging into open models, want to see fit for our customer support triage pipeline. Long transcripts — sometimes meetings plus knowledge base, so really interested in context length.

[00:32] Priya - Arkwave (ML Eng): Yep, and multilingual. We need English and Spanish, maybe Japanese down the line. Also we need tool calling into our ticket DB (internal REST) — function calling or tool-calling work?

[00:48] Nadia (SE): Yeah, Redwood supports both function-style outputs and tool-calling patterns. We often map tool calls to sanitized HTTP connector that can call the ticketing DB. There's a couple ways: send structured function JSON or use an external tool shim; either is supported in Hosted and Dedicated. On Private/on-prem there's more plumbing but doable.
[01:20] Diego - Arkwave (Platform Eng): For Private we'd need VPC peering and KMS — we can't have any PII leave our environment without HSM. Is there an on-prem bundle?

[01:36] Elena (Solutions): Yes, we have Redwood Private which can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem. It can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and audit logs stream to your SIEM. There is an on-prem package but it requires a bit of ops work — Nadia can run through the topology later.

[02:05] Tom: Cool. On models, we've been looking at a few open families — Mistral-like, Llama-derived, and some instruction-tuned 70B variants. Our workload: triage, summarization, and extraction. Accuracy matters but so does cost. Thoughts?

[02:22] Samir: Common pattern — pick a model tier for prod and keep a cheaper fallback for cost-sensitive paths. For extractive tasks you can sometimes use an embeddings + smaller inference model combo. Are you planning to do RAG?

[02:38] Priya: Yes, RAG-ish. We store chunked KB docs and long meeting text. Typical doc lengths push context needs. Some tickets require back-reference to earlier meeting segments — that's why we're thinking 32k or 64k contexts.

[03:00] Nadia: For 32k context, we typically recommend models with verified perf at that length. Redwood's model catalog flags which model builds have 32k or 64k tested profiles. Keep in mind latency and cost scale roughly linearly with sequence length; KV cache helps if you keep prefix context cached for a session.

[03:26] Priya: KV cache — is that the same as the K-V cache? sometimes doc says KV-cache but transcription earlier read it as K V cache, so just making sure it's the key-value cache for attention right?

[03:39] Nadia: Yep K V cache for transformer key/value tensors. Redwood does prefix caching automatically for sessions you pin, which helps if you're reusing the same system prompt or multi-turn conversation. For RAG, we often cache the prompt+retrieved chunks to avoid re-encoding.

[04:00] Tom: Latency targets — we aim for p95 < 800ms for triage classification and < 1.5s for multi-turn summarization. QPS is low-ish (20-40 req/s) but bursty during support surges. Does Redwood Dedicated meet that?

[04:21] Samir: Dedicated is aimed at predictable throughput — you can size GPU pools and get isolation. For your p95 goals, Dedicated with attention-optimized kernels should hit them depending on model size and sequence length; we'll propose config. Hosted can also meet it but might have throttling unless you buy reserved capacity / committed throughput.
[04:44] Diego: Cost — ballpark per-token we're trying to compare. Can you share an apples-to-apples between hosted and dedicated once we give sample prompts?

[04:55] Samir: Absolutely. If you share sample transcripts and expected traffic, we'll run a benchmark and give cost/day for hosted vs ded with reserved capacity. We'll include quantized variants too — smaller-footprint models can reduce cost by 3x-5x.
[05:10] Priya: Multilingual accuracy — do you have language-specific perf profiles? For Spanish we saw some models degrade notably on extraction tasks.

[05:23] Nadia: We maintain per-language evaluations for a lot of open models. Some models are instruction-tuned primarily on English and need localized fine-tuning or instruction datasets. For Spanish we can recommend models with better cross-lingual pretraining or propose a small fine-tune/eval loop as part of the POC.
[05:46] Tom: Tool-calling: we want the model to open a ticket, or summarise and then call our enrichment API to attach metadata. How deterministic is tool-calling vs hallucination?

[06:00] Nadia: Tool calling is as deterministic as you make it — if you whitelist functions and validate arguments server-side, the actual API call happens only once validated. We recommend a validation layer to avoid malformed payloads. Redwood also supports dry-run mode for function outputs so you can preview calls.
[06:22] Priya: Security — SOC2 is required, and we need audit logs with user attribution. Also data retention policies for logs. Can Dedicated and Hosted both provide those?

[06:35] Elena: Hosted is SOC2 compliant and we offer audit logs, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC. For Dedicated you get more isolation and you can opt for longer retention as part of enterprise add-on. For Private/on-prem you control retention and logs entirely.
[07:00] Tom: Ok. A few nitty gritty: does Redwood do model rollouts/canarying? We want safe-rollouts so we can compare variants on real traffic.

[07:12] Samir: Yes rollouts and canarying are part of the console. You can A/B by route, send a percent of traffic to new model, and set auto-fallback if quality drops. Also we expose token-level cost and latency per route.
[07:32] Diego: On-prem testing — how intrusive is the on-prem package? We need to know what ports/agents and whether it requires persistent outbound to Redwood control plane.

[07:48] Nadia: Private can run with a customer-managed control plane; in locked-down modes we support air-gapped deployment but there is some setup overhead. For standard VPC mode, you get a private control plane connecting over peered VPC, no customer data leaves your network unencrypted. We'll send a topology doc.
[08:12] Tom: Benchmarks — what's the plan?

[08:18] Samir: Two-step: 1) run hosted baseline across 3 candidate models on your sample prompts (we'll provide an instrumented harness), 2) spin a small Dedicated config for the best candidate to measure p95 and cost at scale. We'll share the perf spreadsheet and raw logs.
[08:38] Priya: For the sample prompts — do you accept raw transcripts or do we need to chunk them?
[08:44] Nadia: Raw is fine, we'll handle chunking in the bench harness. But include expected metadata (timestamps, speaker labels) so we can reproduce your exact RAG flow.
[09:00] Tom: One more: latency vs quality tradeoff — if we quantize models, do we see big extraction accuracy drops?

[09:12] Nadia: Quantization depends on model family. Some 4-bit quantization schemes are very good for generative tasks; for sensitive extraction you might prefer 8-bit or a distilled smaller model plus reranker. We'll include recommended quantization profiles in the perf doc.
[09:36] Diego: Are there existing customers doing multilingual + tool-calling in production? Any reference architecture?
[09:45] Elena: Yes — a couple of customers in EMEA are running multi-lingual support bots with tool-calling to CRMs. We'll anonymize and share an architecture case study link after the call.
[10:05] Priya: How do you handle session-level caching with multitenant hosted? If user has long conversation history, do you keep the full prefix in memory?

[10:18] Nadia: For hosted multitenant we use TTL-based prefix caching and LRU eviction. For Dedicated you can reserve more cache and pin sessions for lower latency. We can tune autoscaling to retain warm workers for bursty loads.
[10:35] Tom: Ok great. Anything else from Arkwave?
[10:39] Priya: We'll share our PII redaction rules too; we need to ensure masked content doesn't break extractions.
[10:50] Samir: Noted. We'll include guidance on in-pipeline redaction and best practices. Any timing constraints for the pilot?
[10:58] Tom: We'd like to start a POC in the next 3 weeks, ideally a 2-week pilot. So if you can get benchmarks back the week after next that works.
[11:08] Samir: Sounds doable. We'll follow-up with calendar invites for the bench run and an SE deep dive for the on-prem questions. I'll attach pricing comparatives.
[11:18] Diego: Also share SLA tiers for Dedicated and Private, and details on failover policies.

[11:24] Elena: We'll attach the SLA doc and the failover patterns. Quick note: we support automated fallback to smaller model families if a high-cost model runs out of capacity — that is transparent in the routing policy.
[11:44] Tom: Great. Thanks everyone. Quick recap?

[11:50] Samir: Recap: Arkwave to share samples and latency targets; Redwood to run hosted bench across candidate open models for 32k context, propose Dedicated config for pilot, share pricing and security docs, schedule on-prem deep-dive. Action owners noted in follow-ups.
[12:15] Priya: One small question — do you have any plugins for our ticketing system (they use Ticketrix internal)?
[12:24] Nadia: We don't have an out-of-the-box Ticketrix plugin but the connector SDK is lightweight. We can prototype a connector during the POC.
[12:40] Tom: Perfect. We'll wait for the perf spreadsheet. Thanks all.
[12:45] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up. Bye.
notes: Artifacts mentioned: pricing spreadsheet (link sent post-call), architecture case study (will be shared), topology doc for Private deployments. Some transcriptions show small name errors (Ticketrix sometimes transcribed as Ticket-ricks).
raw_transcript_notes: Transcription quirks: Redwood Dedicated often transcribed as Red-Wood Dedicated in older exports; KV cache sometimes split as K V cache; function-calling also appears as function callin in places. Occasional filler words and overlap in speakers caused minor mislabels.
file_notes: Bench harness and perf spreadsheet to be stored in deal folder CRM-ARW-2028-07; follow-up SE deep-dive invite to be scheduled after receipt of sample data.
